input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN running against us: we must give Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms we offer any other technology supplier. It is not limited to a defined product, has no 12-month cap and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory (open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better terms given to third parties). It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so deleting the clause reaches the preferred position without disturbing any benefit to us.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the open-ended obligation for us to extend Vendor the best terms we offer any other supplier; our playbook does not accept MFN obligations running against the customer, and this clause also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2
